title: How the Policy Engine Decides
summary: Every transaction is looked up in a rulebook, and the matching rule decides.
lesson: The guard finds the one matching rule and its policy decides; anything unmatched goes to Anything else.
oneLiner: Every transaction is looked up in a rulebook, and the matching rule decides.
explain: Every Safe transaction goes to the Policy Guard first. The guard looks it up in the rulebook by contract, action and call type.
The matching rule names one policy, the checker that decides. Changing the rulebook later takes a waiting period.
No matching rule? The Anything else row decides. Without that row, the transaction is blocked.
takeaway: The guard finds the one matching rule and its policy decides; anything unmatched goes to Anything else.

steps.label: Pay Dave 500 USDC
steps.note: The USDC rule names the Recipient Allowlist, and Dave is on it.

steps.label: Pay Mallory 500 USDC
steps.note: The same rule decides, and Mallory is not on the USDC list.

steps.label: Send Erin 1 ETH, co-signed
steps.note: No rule mentions ETH, so Anything else decides. It asks the co-signer, who agreed.

steps.label: In one batch: pay Dave 500 USDC and send Erin 1 ETH, co-signed
steps.note: The batch has a rule of its own. Then each step is checked like a separate transaction, and both pass.

steps.label: Pay Erin 500 USDC, co-signed
steps.note: USDC has its own rule, so Anything else is never asked. The co-signer cannot add Erin to the list.
